title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.conditional: Documented, with plan, policy or endpoint conditions.
definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.
definitions.not_supported: Vendor documentation states this credential lacks the control.
definitions.unknown: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_verified: No source found either way. Not a negative finding.
definitions.not_applicable: Does not apply to this credential.
definitions.limited: Documented for a narrower case only.

providers.name: PingOne
providers.scope_notes: Covers PingOne (PingOne Platform / Management APIs). SaaS; covers PingOne platform Worker apps and gateway credentials; inbound traffic policies need a Cloudflare-based custom domain.

controls.name: Delete Gateway Credentials
controls.what: Deletes and revokes a gateway credential for all instances using it.

controls.name: Environment Admin role required for gateway entities
controls.what: Only admins with the Environment Admin role can create or manage gateway credentials.

controls_unknown: Whether disabling the app or rotating the secret invalidates already-issued access tokens (role removal does take effect per call per S5)
Whether successful client_credentials token issuance produces an audit event
Whether Management API read calls (e.g., GET users) are audited
Whether inbound traffic policies apply to api.pingone.com
Admin-level policy to block Worker app creation or require approval
Gateway credential expiry and whether its creation/deletion has a distinct audit event
Maximum configurable access token lifetime for the PingOne API resource

authentication.summary: A gateway instance (LDAP, PingFederate, RADIUS, API gateway integration, Authorize) running in the customer's infrastructure holds a signed JWT gateway credential. It exchanges the credential at /as/token (token_exchange grant) for an access token to PingOne resources.

federation.details: Static signed JWT issued by PingOne.

ip_restriction.boundary: No IP restriction documented for gateway credentials.

lifetime.summary: No expiry documented; claims list has no exp claim

renewal.expiry_basis: Create a new credential (max five per gateway) and delete the old one
renewal.summary: Rotation is manual by issuing a new credential.

administration.summary: Environment Admins create, list, and delete gateway credentials. Deleting a credential revokes it for all gateway instances using it.
administration.conditions: Max five credentials per gateway; token value shown only at creation.

offboard.details: The credential belongs to a gateway instance, not a user.

inventory.details: GET /v1/environments/{envID}/gateways/{gatewayID}/credentials lists credentials per gateway (max five per gateway).

token_format.notes: Signed JWT; iss wss://gateways.pingone.com; jti equals the credential ID.

log_sources.name: PingOne Audit (Monitoring > Audit) and GET/POST /v1/environments/{envID}/activities
log_sources.notes: Configuration events kept 2 years, user events 90 days; queries max 14 days; Audit API rate 10/second.

log_sources.name: Subscriptions (webhooks)
log_sources.notes: Streams audit events to HTTPS/TCP endpoints; events lost if target down >7 days.

anomaly_cues: lastUsedAt changes on a credential for a decommissioned gateway
More credentials than running gateway instances

containment.notes: Docs say all instances using it lose their credentials; already-exchanged access tokens not addressed.

unknown: What the exchanged token can read
